newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmen head promises citizens higher pay.
newsitem.headline: Turkmen head promises citizens higher pay.

text.p: Salaries of Turkmen state-paid employees and the military will be doubled from March 1, Turkmenistan's president, Saparmurat Niyazov, has pledged.
Speaking on television late on Tuesday, Niyazov said a total of $92 million was being earmarked to raise salaries which average just 100,000 manats ($18) a month.
"When we resolve some organisational problems, pensions and scholarships will be increased as well," Niyazov promised his desert nation of 3.8 million people.
Turkmenistan, where Niyazov enjoys a Soviet-era personality cult, remains one of the poorest republics of the former Soviet Union although it has huge reserves of natural gas and oil.
Niyazov said the increase of salaries would be at the expense of several former Soviet republics having debts for Turkmen gas.

"The increase is due to fines imposed on Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan for overdue payments for Turkmen gas delivered to them in 1994-1996," he said, promising that higher salaries would not spur up inflation.
"We expect that in 1997 these states will pay out a total of $184 million, and a half of this sum will be used to increase the well-being of the population," Niyazov said.
He added he hoped that converting dollars in the country's central bank before paying salaries would "also positively influence the stability of the Turkmen manat currency".
